question: Is the air better in the north or the west of Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
The air is noticeably better in the **north** right now, though it's still unhealthy across Singapore because of the haze.

The newest readings I found are NEA figures for **17 October, 12:00 pm**, shown on hazenow.app:

| Region | 1‑hr PM2.5 (the air right now) | 24‑hr PSI |
|---|---|---|
| **North** | 91 µg/m³ (Elevated) | 136 (Unhealthy) |
| **West** | 206 µg/m³ (High) | 178 (Unhealthy) |

- **The north is better on both readings.** Its PM2.5 for the last hour is less than half the west's. At that point the west had the worst air of any region in Singapore.
- **The west has been hit harder all week.** On 14 October its hourly PM2.5 reached 288, the highest reading in Singapore since 2015. Earlier readings from 16 and 17 October also showed the north as the cleanest region.

**What to do:** Even in the north, the 24‑hr PSI is in the "Unhealthy" range. NEA's current advice is for the general public to avoid strenuous outdoor activity. Elderly people, pregnant women, children, and anyone with heart or lung conditions should avoid all outdoor activity.

These readings are updated every hour and conditions can change quickly. I've hit my search limit, so I couldn't get anything newer than noon. Before you head out, check the latest 1‑hr PM2.5 for each region at **haze.gov.sg**.
